question: How much does learner history improve next-response prediction?
method: Learner-disjoint train/validation/test; priors, BKT, PFA and GRU; predict before updating with the current answer.
interpretation: After a response, Bayes updating and the learning transition produce the next mastery state. Brier and log loss assess probabilities; learner-block bootstrap respects within-learner dependence. Model mastery is not directly measured knowledge.
status: RECORDED EXTERNAL-DATA STUDY | full experiment not rerun in this review
table_title: Selected recorded values (units and context shown)
evidence_note: Selected committed results; source values were not independently retrained in this review.
finding: On 623 held-out learners, the seed-42 GRU achieves ROC-AUC 0.7470 and Brier score 0.1800, compared with 0.6982 and 0.1976 for PFA. The three GRU seeds average ROC-AUC 0.7471 with sample SD 0.0008. These results support better response prediction under this historical benchmark; they do not establish instructional benefit or justify high-stakes interpretations of a learner’s knowledge.
